principles.authority: Only cranium-kernel may evaluate, reduce, replay-protect, journal, persist canonical state, issue canonical receipts, or grant authority.
principles.evidence: Synapse and all supporting surfaces provide bounded evidence or requests; evidence never grants authority.
principles.state: Canonical state is loaded from and committed through the Kernel authority proxy/store; browser state, local reducers, fixtures, and model output are non-canonical.
principles.failure: Ambiguous, stale, tampered, replay-conflicting, unverifiable, or non-durable operations fail closed.
principles.claims: Evidence language must distinguish implemented and verified, implemented not yet verified in CI, designed not implemented, fixture/test-only, and placeholder. Placeholders are prohibited in authority-bearing data.

transition.replay: exact reuse returns the committed transition; conflicting reuse is rejected
transition.commit: only a boundary-passing evaluation may be reduced and durably committed

evidenceLabels: implemented, not yet verified in CI

conformance.nonGoal: Byte-identical local filesystem behavior across platforms is not required; logical authority semantics must not drift.
